children: United Parcel Service is set to report third-quarter results before the market opens Tuesday. Here is what you need to know.
PROFIT: The Atlanta-based carrier is projected to post a profit of $1.36 billion, compared with $1.31 billion in the same period last year, according to analysts polled by FactSet.
ADJUSTED EARNINGS: Stripping out one-time items, earnings are expected to come in at $1.62 a share. That compares with adjusted earnings of $1.74 a share a year earlier.
REVENUE: Quarterly revenue is forecast to be $22.27 billion, up from $21.4 billion last year.
The stock is down 12% over the past three months and was recently trading hands at $100.60.

UPS is working to rejig its operating model, shaking up its executive team last month as it takes steps to standardize operational processes across geographies. The company promoted Nando Cesarone to lead the new model as chief global operations officer, while additionally promoting Matt Guffey as chief U.S. domestic officer. Investors will be looking to see how these new appointments are helping shape the company's trajectory.

The executive shake-up is part of UPS's work to evolve into an integrated logistics solutions provider from a small package carrier, as well as a key piece of its effort to accelerate profitable growth, the company previously said. UPS has been wrapping up a years-long restructuring effort that included a rollback of package delivery for some e-commerce companies like Amazon, as well as cutting tens of thousands of delivery-driver and warehouse-worker roles. Investors will be on the lookout for updates regarding this transformation.

Improving retail sales trends and accelerating Chinese exports point to a more constructive revenue outlook for UPS, Evercore analysts said in a research note. At the same time, though, the Amazon glide down has resulted in lower volume run rates and is likely to weigh on year-over-year comparisons. "Moreover, the largely fuel-driven nature of the revenue upside limits the earnings benefit, with higher fuel costs tempering operating leverage in our forecasts," the analysts said, maintaining their profit outlook despite higher revenue expectations.
